plan_title: Sharad Pitta-Shamana and Prameha-Supportive Daily Pathya
plan_description: This day is built for Sharad ritucharya with Pitta-pacifying, diabetes-friendly foods while keeping meals regular for Sama Agni. Barley, moong, bitter gourd, amla, pomegranate, and steady dairy/soy support glycemic control, heart health, and B12 coverage without excess heaviness.

pathya: Barley — light, ruksha and astringent, it supports Prameha management and is preferred in Langhana.
Yellow Moong Dal — easy to digest, supports protein needs, and is classically suitable in Prameha.
Bitter Gourd — bitter taste and light quality help pacify Pitta and support glucose balance.
Amla — sour-sweet-astringent with cooling virya, ideal in Sharad and supportive for Hridroga and Prameha.
Pomegranate — cooling, astringent and heart-supportive, useful in Pitta aggravation.
Cow's Milk — taken in moderate quantity with meals, it supports daily B12 intake for metformin users.
Tofu — light vegetarian protein that helps meet protein targets without excess saturated fat.
Fenugreek Seed — bitter, ruksha and helpful for Prameha when used in small amounts.
Coriander Seed — cooling and Pitta-pacifying, useful for seasoning without excess salt or heat.
Fennel — mild, cooling and digestive, suitable for regular meals in Pitta vikriti.
apathya: White Rice / Rice, raw in large quantity — too heavy and glycemic for Prameha, and white rice is specifically avoided.
Sugar and jaggery in excess — aggravate Madhumeha and increase meda.
Deep-fried foods — increase heaviness, salt load and Pitta disturbance, and are unfavorable in Hridroga.
Excess sour, salty, pungent foods — worsen Sharad Pitta aggravation.
Daytime napping — a primary lifestyle apathya in Prameha.
Irregular meal timing or fasting — can destabilize glucose and is not suitable here without medical advice.
viruddha_ahara_warnings: Milk with sour fruits such as amla or pomegranate in the same preparation — milk and sour substances are traditionally incompatible and may disturb digestion.
Curd with fruit or at night in excess — curd is kapha-increasing and can aggravate Prameha; avoid incompatible combinations and heavy evening use.
Heating honey — classical texts advise against heating honey because it becomes incompatible and is considered harmful.
pathya_apathya.classical_reference: Charaka Sutrasthana 6.41 for Sharad Pitta management; Charaka Chikitsa Sthana 6 for Prameha pathya-apathya; Charaka Chikitsa 26 and Sushruta Uttara 43 for Hridroga; classical viruddha-ahara principles from Ayurveda.

therapeutic_arc.basis: Ama none, build normal, diabetes. Apatarpana is the line of treatment; no Santarpana phase is scheduled.
withheld: Brimhana — the fixed progression put a nourishing week with ghee, nuts and root vegetables at week 3. Charaka Sutrasthana 23 names Prameha, Medoroga and Kushtha as diseases of over-nourishment; adding Santarpana to them is the cause, not the treatment.

weeks.focus: Kindling — warming spices, regular timing, nothing heavy
weeks.rationale: No significant Ama, so the first week goes straight to Agni.

weeks.focus: Reducing — lighter meals, barley and millets over wheat and rice, no late eating
weeks.rationale: Reduce Meda and Kapha while Agni is now able to carry it.

weeks.focus: Drying — astringent and bitter tastes, minimal oil, honey over sugar
weeks.rationale: Rukshana addresses the Snigdha quality underlying Medoroga.

weeks.focus: Holding — a sustainable version of weeks 2-3, seasonally adjusted
weeks.rationale: Consolidate rather than rebound; this is the week the plan has to outlive.

condition_coaching: For diabetes, keep carbohydrate portions steady across the day and favor barley, moong, bitter gourd, amla, and fenugreek rather than rice-heavy meals. For heart health, keep salt modest, avoid fried foods and heavy dairy, and include pomegranate, amla, and barley regularly. Because the patient uses metformin and warfarin, include a consistent small daily amount of leafy greens and a daily dairy/fortified food portion, and avoid sudden large changes in these foods.
hydration_guidance: Aim for 1 to 2 liters of fluids through the day, mostly warm or room-temperature water, green tea, tulsi tea, or light cumin-coriander-fennel infused water if desired. Sip between meals rather than taking large volumes with meals; avoid sugary drinks and keep tender coconut water occasional and small because of diabetes.
fasting_guidance: Do not do fasting days. Keep regular meal times every day; if any therapeutic fast is ever considered, it should be discussed with the treating doctor because of diabetes and medication use.
seasonal_note: Sharad is a Pitta-aggravating season, so favor cooling, sweet, bitter, and astringent foods such as amla, pomegranate, cucumber, bottle gourd, bitter gourd, and barley. Keep spices gentle and avoid excess sourness, salt, and pungency.
ahar_vidhi: Eat at fixed times and do not skip meals, since Sama Agni is strong but diabetes needs regularity. Prefer freshly cooked, warm, lightly spiced food with minimal oil and moderate salt. Keep the largest meal at lunch, and make dinner lighter than lunch but still complete.
motivational_note: Steady, simple meals will support your sugar control, heart health, and seasonal balance without overburdening digestion.
